name: Payslip Check
tagline: Automated Israeli payslip auditing in plain Hebrew
oneLiner: A Hebrew, RTL web system that reads a payslip, extracts its data, runs it through a rules engine based on Israeli labour law and extension orders, and returns a clear verdict — valid or needs review — with per-finding explanations and estimated monetary gaps.
audience: Private employees checking their own payslip, and payroll professionals checking clients' payslips

extraction: AI OCR + structured extraction (Gemini / OpenAI / Anthropic)

highlights: Extensible rules engine: 17 independent rule modules, each returning findings and follow-up questions; adding a check is one file plus one registry line
Every finding carries actual vs. expected vs. gap, a legal source, a confidence level, an explanation, and an estimated monetary impact split into high-certainty vs. estimate
Honest by design: when data is insufficient the engine returns 'cannot determine' and asks one targeted follow-up question instead of asserting an error
Date-versioned legal parameters (minimum wage, convalescence day value, pension rates, travel caps) resolved by the payslip month, each tagged with an effectiveFrom and a confidence
Managed legal parameters editable in-app override the code constants, so yearly updates need no redeploy
Structured AI extraction returns the payslip as typed JSON directly, far more accurate than parsing raw text, with per-use model and cost logging
Runtime-selected storage: file repository or PostgreSQL chosen automatically by the presence of DATABASE_URL, behind one repository interface
Sensitive documents encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM; owner isolation on every check; national-ID masking in list views
Four-step wizard (upload, verify, follow-up questions, results) with a manual verification screen so heuristic extraction errors never silently corrupt a check
features: Dual mode: private employee, or professional managing per-client setting cards auto-filled into new checks
Upload payslip (required) plus optional attendance report and employment contract
Automatic extraction with a manual verification/correction screen for every field and line

Rules covered: minimum wage, overtime (125%/150%/global), pension, convalescence, annual vacation, sick pay, severance accrual, holiday pay, contract bonus, study fund, income-tax sanity, split-rate, travel, teaching-sector degree & seniority, attendance cross-check, gross/net/deduction consistency
Detailed printable report grouped by category, saveable as PDF
Multi-payslip comparison across months with gross/net trends and total estimated gap
Personal settings and per-client setting cards for auto-fill
Admin: user management, view-as (read-only), audit log, AI/OCR settings, managed legal parameters, and a usage & cost screen per user and model
Optional AI anomaly scan layer on top of the deterministic rules
engineeringDecisions: Model each labour-law check as an independent Rule object behind a single RuleContext, so the domain grows by addition, not modification
Separate deterministic law parameters (date-versioned, confidence-tagged) from the rules that consume them
Prefer 'cannot determine' + a follow-up question over a false positive when inputs are incomplete
Abstract storage behind a repository interface with file and PostgreSQL implementations selected at runtime
Inject the OCR/extraction provider so the app degrades gracefully to manual entry when no provider is configured
Encrypt documents at rest and mask identifiers in the UI, treating payslips as sensitive personal data
